page: Microsoft Azure D32ds_v4 is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the DDSv4 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL x86_64 processor running at 2.6 GHz, configured with 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs via hyper-threading under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, it includes a bundled 1229 GB local SSD and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark evaluations place the D32ds_v4 consistently in the average tier across most workloads. The instance achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 10969.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 27517.37. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 1663.77 GB/sec, which drops to 107.43 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Cryptographic and vector operations are supported by hardware flags including AES, AVX, and AVX512.

Tradeoffs are evident in single-threaded operations and large-scale computations. Single-threaded gzip compression is weak at 23.52 GB/sec, and prompt processing for a large 70B LLM model drops to a weak 5.64 tokens/sec. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 131.5 GB/sec, and database operations score 10619.72 on Passmark. This profile makes the instance appropriate for balanced workloads such as database operations, static web serving, software compilation, and medium-scale text or image processing.
description: Microsoft Azure D32ds_v4 is a general-purpose server from the DDSv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8272CL x86_64 processor with 32 vCPUs, 16 physical cores, and 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance includes a 1229 GB local SSD and supports Premium Storage. Performance benchmarks generally fall within the average range, with a Passmark CPU score of 27517.37 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 10969.0. While single-threaded gzip compression and large-model LLM inference show weaker performance, the server demonstrates solid capabilities in multi-threaded tasks, such as bzip3 decompression at 131.5 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 27.94 million operations per second. This hardware profile is suitable for database operations, software compilation, static web serving, and general-purpose enterprise workloads.
